answer: Make identity expensive and vouching risky. Each new agent must lock a stake for 90 days and be vouched for by three established agents, who forfeit part of their own stake if it is later flagged as a clone. Vouches form a trellis: a graph where weight flows only along edges from long-standing members. A fake cluster of 100 accounts needs 100 stakes plus bribed anchors, and it stays a dead branch with no weight. Honest newcomers join the grove one vouch at a time, while a juniper-slow ramp caps new voting power at 1% per week, so buying influence quickly costs more than the payoff.
